summary.title: Career advice I wish I'd been given when I was young
summary.one_liner: An anonymous, highly experienced policy professional shares seventeen career tips, such as building a resume through parallel side projects, cold-emailing admired thinkers, prioritising neglected existential risks, and treating time as more valuable than money.
takeaways: Build a standout resume by taking on several parallel part-time or volunteer projects rather than planning a rigid long-term path.
Cold-email admired thinkers and employers, and use mutual contacts to vouch for you.
Prioritise neglected, high-impact problems such as existential risk, and be sceptical of earning-to-give careers.
Value your time highly, use satisficing for most decisions, and be pleasant to work with, especially in policy settings.
summary.summary: This 80,000 Hours article republishes a list of seventeen career tips from an anonymous reader whose career the editors considered impactful. The advice is aimed at people sympathetic to effective altruism, especially those interested in public policy, though the editors say much of it applies more broadly. Each tip is a short personal reflection, with editor notes linking to related articles and a reading list of nuclear and institutional-disaster books in the footnotes. The piece is opinion and anecdote rather than a structured tutorial.
